Bowtie 2 2.4.2: bowtie2-build-s, bowtie2-align-s
Licence: GPL-3.0 (LICENSE in this folder). Built with zlib 1.3.2 (ZLIB-LICENSE).
Upstream source: https://github.com/BenLangmead/bowtie2/tree/v2.4.2 (commit 8be3a210eb488610072de14449eccf9b041d8930)

These two programs were compiled to WebAssembly for this practical – they are not Biowasm builds.
Compiler: Emscripten 6.0.10; WebAssembly SIMD for Bowtie 2's SSE2 code; WebAssembly exceptions; no threads.
Everything needed to build them again is in ../../../licenses/:
  sources/bowtie2-2.4.2.tar.xz              the source of the release (git archive of the tag v2.4.2)
  bowtie2-build/bowtie2-v2.4.2-webassembly.patch   the changes made to it (Makefile, bt2_build.cpp, bt2_search.cpp, pat.cpp)
  bowtie2-build/build-bowtie2.sh            the build script (it also records exit(status) in the loaders)
  bowtie2-build/README.txt                  how to run it

Changes to the source (all in the patch): the Makefile builds with em++; the aligner runs its search
in the calling thread; bowtie2-build ignores --threads above 1, with a note; one buffer is cleared
so that the program can be run again in the same page; and a read file that cannot be opened is
reported as on Linux ("Could not open read file", exit status 1 – the C library of this build takes
the descriptor of a file that was not opened without complaint, so the aligner has to look itself;
bowtie2-align-s was built again with this change on 5 October 2026, bowtie2-build-s is the build of
2 October).

In the terminal of the practical, "bowtie2" runs bowtie2-align-s and "bowtie2-build" runs
bowtie2-build-s, each with --wrapper basic-0 as the wrapper scripts of Bowtie 2 do. The wrapper
scripts themselves (perl, python) are not here. What the wrapper of bowtie2 does around the aligner,
the terminal does in its place: it looks for the index first ("(ERR): "NAME" does not exist or is
not a Bowtie 2 index", exit status 255) and reports a failure of the aligner ("(ERR): bowtie2-align
exited with value N"). The options that the wrapper carries out itself (--un, --al, --un-conc,
--al-conc and their -gz/-bz2/-lz4 forms) are not available; large indexes (-l) are not needed.

Checked against a native build of the same version: the index of the course reference is identical,
byte for byte. Reads with two equally good positions can be placed at the other one (21 of 3,519
pairs of the course data): Bowtie 2 breaks such ties with a pseudo-random number, and that differs
between this 32-bit build and a 64-bit one. The variants called from both are the same 50 (positions,
alleles, genotypes); two of the 50 lines differ in QUAL or DP.
